versions.title: Microsoft accounts, multiple game folders, per-version Java
log: Microsoft sign-in has been rebuilt: save several accounts, switch or remove them at any time, and stay signed in after restarting the launcher
Sign-in tokens refresh automatically before launch; if a token expires, the launcher now asks you to sign in again instead of failing when joining a server
Saved accounts show their real Minecraft skin head
Add several game folders and filter versions by folder; choosing a parent folder such as a PCL2 root automatically finds the .minecraft inside it
Each version can use its own Java runtime: automatic, 8, 16, 17, 21, 25 or a custom path
Crash analysis now speaks all 25 languages, and error reports include your time zone and local time
The download panel shows a live speed graph, current and peak speed and queued tasks; speed can be displayed in MB/s or Mbps
Java runtime downloads moved to their own tab on the download page
Memory usage on the settings page now refreshes live instead of showing the value from when the page was opened
Deleting the selected version returns to the version list immediately instead of still showing the deleted version

versions.title: A rebuilt download page, with modpacks and shaders
log: Download progress now lives at the bottom of the window: stay on whatever page you are on, the bar shows the current file, progress and speed, and it opens into the full download queue where you can cancel at any time
The download page now has Shaders, Resource packs and Modpacks tabs: Modrinth and CurseForge modpacks install in one click, local archives can be imported, and NeoForge is supported
Version isolation is now an explicit setting: each version gets its own mods, saves and settings by default, with five levels to choose from and a per-version switch
You can name a version while downloading it, creating a separate instance so different mod setups do not interfere with each other
Mod search is much faster: All sources now runs in parallel with compression, repeated searches hit the cache, and Chinese searches look up the English name in a wiki first
Mod search sorts by relevance with sources interleaved; the detail page shows where the Chinese name came from, and you can add custom mod sources and name dictionaries in Settings
Mod loaders are now mutually exclusive: picking Forge marks the others as incompatible, and the install target list only shows compatible versions with the destination written on the button
Fixed truncated downloads, slow cancellation and the main window not updating after deleting a version; first-time installs no longer play the intro animation

versions.title: Twenty-five languages, from the launcher to the website
log: GoodPlanCraftLauncher now speaks 25 languages: pick one under Settings → Appearance → Interface language, and search the list to find it quickly
On first launch it follows your system language, and the welcome guide lets you choose one before doing anything else
A new welcome guide walks through language, interface style, and a short introduction in four steps, and can be skipped
Three interface styles: Minecraft, Advanced (the familiar look), and Minimal
The installer is translated into the same 25 languages and picks your system language automatically
The help center is available in 25 languages, and help links in the launcher open the page matching your interface language
The website and the interactive demo inside it are available in 25 languages as well
Arabic, Persian, and Hebrew switch the whole interface to right-to-left layout
Startup no longer flashes: the splash screen and the main window are one page, and the window background follows your theme; switching languages reloads without a black frame

versions.title: Custom avatars, and a version list you can search
log: You can now change the launch screen avatar: click it, or pick an image under Settings → Appearance → Avatar; PNG / JPG / GIF / WebP are supported
Images over 1 MB ask whether to compress; the limit is 4 MB, and the default avatar can be restored in one click
Appearance settings add an 'Avatar size' slider, 32–160 pixels
The version list gains a search box; each version shows its game version and mod loader, and the selected one is highlighted
Refreshing the version list no longer rebuilds it, so the scroll position stays put; 'Import local version' moved to the top right of the list
On 1.20 and later, choosing 'Join server' connects directly; a missing address now shows a prompt instead of quietly starting singleplayer
Version settings autosave no longer pops up 'Saved' every time
The installer shrank from about 103 MB to 93 MB: only Chinese and English language packs are kept, with other languages falling back to English
1.7.1 was an unreleased internal test build and has been withdrawn; 1.7.2 includes all of its changes

versions.title: Shaders, resource packs, and modpacks, installed in one click
log: The download page adds Shaders and Resource packs tabs: search Modrinth / CurseForge and install straight into the matching folder for the chosen version
A new Modpacks tab supports Modrinth (.mrpack) and CurseForge modpacks, installing the matching game version, mod loader, and all mods automatically
Each modpack becomes its own version, with mods, configs, and saves in its own folder, so modpacks do not mix into each other
Local modpacks can be imported too: pick a zip / .mrpack in version management, enter a name, and installation starts
Modpack files are checked against the manifest for size and SHA1, so half-downloaded jars are fetched again instead of producing a game that will not start
NeoForge can now be installed by version like Forge / Fabric (1.20.1 and later)
The 'More' menu is collapsed by default; enable it under Settings → Appearance when needed, and the bug where it reappeared after a restart has been fixed

versions.title: Crash reasons, told straight
log: Crashes are diagnosed automatically (out of memory, wrong Java version, missing dependencies, GPU drivers, OptiFine / Forge incompatibility, and more), and the dialog gives 1–2 conclusions
'View details' shows every clue and evidence line; 'View logs' opens the game directory of the version that crashed

Error reports export a complete zip: analysis results, error summary, system and GPU, Java version, version and mod loader, mods / resource packs / shaders lists, launch arguments, game output, and crash reports
The report redacts --accessToken and the system username, so it can be sent to others for troubleshooting
With several games running at once, each session keeps its own output, so a crash context never bleeds into another version

The mod details page was rebuilt: Chinese and English names, download counts, category tags, file lists grouped by MC version, dependency cards, links to Modrinth / CurseForge / MCMod, and one-click name copying
Fixed dependencies for a 1.20.1 install being resolved as 1.20, which duplicated Fabric API / GeckoLib versions and made Fabric report Incompatible mods found and refuse to start
Installing a mod removes old jars of the same project, so multiple versions no longer pile up

versions.title: Install mods without hunting for files
log: The download page adds a Mods tab: search Modrinth / CurseForge, pick files for the current game version, and choose which version to install into
Modrinth pulls in required dependencies automatically; Chinese search is supported (the query goes through MCMod to get the English name first)
It also works without a CurseForge API key: paste a project link or cf:slug and install a single file through the mirror
Downloads are now a task queue: clicking several versions queues them, queued tasks can be removed, and cancelling the current one lets the queue continue
Auto-update now installs silently: it downloads in the background and installs when you exit the launcher, with a round badge in the top right showing progress
New: automatic game language (Simplified Chinese by default), a custom game directory, and a custom file mirror
New: import a local version from a version folder or zip / jar
Fabric actually installs now, with Fabric API by default; with version isolation, mods and saves follow the version
Forge installation only runs --installClient, shows progress, and says plainly when the Java version is too old
OptiFine installs silently instead of opening the graphical installer
Fixed zero-byte downloads counting as success, relative-address redirects, and the second download showing no progress

versions.title: Settings, rebuilt
log: The settings page was rebuilt: memory, window, launch behavior, download sources, and Java arguments are regrouped, adjustable with sliders, switches, and segmented buttons
Memory now defaults to 'Auto': 30% of physical memory, at least 1 GB and at most 8 GB, leaving 2 GB for the system; it can also be set manually
Memory management actually reclaims now: it only cleans the launcher's own processes, never a running game, and can be set to optimize automatically before launch
Download sources have four modes (auto / mirror first / official first / official only), chosen separately for files and version lists; a 0–20 MB/s global speed limit was added
New: G1GC tuning, custom JVM arguments, process priority, window size presets, and launcher visibility
The About page now covers project information, the runtime environment, and the full license; the website and help pages were rewritten too
Fixed: the thread count setting being ignored, 404 pages being saved as files, and partial files left behind after failed downloads

versions.title: It crashed? Let me look
log: New crash notice: when the game exits abnormally it explains why, with one-click error reports (crash report + logs + system info, tokens redacted)
New running panel: after launch it shows the version, PID, uptime, and memory on the right, and can end the game at any time
The username field keeps the last 5 names in a dropdown, each removable
The game now runs in its own process, so closing the launcher no longer ends it; closing the game window is also recognized as an exit
New custom game window titles with magic words ({mc_version}, {time}, and more)
Launch tips now appear at random (configurable in settings), with many more entries added
Smoother startup animation and page transitions

versions.title: Java fixed, and a fresh new look
log: Fixed Java runtime downloads: a changed mirror file name broke installation, so it is now fetched dynamically
The installer moved to Inno Setup and upgrades in place from older versions
Unified global colors (sky blue as the main color, deep blue for dark mode), with a new startup animation and website
Fixed the startup screen ignoring the light theme and several button styles not applying

versions.title: Shader support!
log: Added OptiFine (shader) support
One-click installation that handles inheritance, libraries, and tweakClass automatically
Supports the inheritsFrom version inheritance mechanism

versions.title: Fixed
log: Fixed the double scrollbar issue
Expanded the About page with more content, including a toolbox

versions.title: Fixed? I doubt it
log: The splash screen had some issues in the last version
Brought settings into order
Cancelling a launch now actually kills the process!

versions.title: Welcome!
log: Added a welcome animation on first launch
Removed excessive anti-debugging and allowed developer mode

versions.title: Taking off!
log: Attempted to actually support Forge
Instant start! This is an installer build, compiled to machine code!
Fixed bugs, thanks to the forum
Greatly streamlined the flow; update details can now show a full log
Forge / Fabric / OptiFine actually work now!
This is the first open source release!
Added detailed per-version settings, managed by default; game versions can be deleted
More light mode support; 'Restore defaults' moved into a new compatibility settings section; API updated
Polished dropdowns and various other details
Fixed the missing download chart (it was not called in the installed build)
Moved the automatic update check setting to About
The download page now lists Alpha, Beta, snapshots, and releases in full, fixing release versions not being fully shown
Rebuilt the launch screen, adding version management sorted by last launch time
Added 'Did you know?' tips at startup and automatic log cleanup (the interval can be changed in settings)
Interface scaling under Appearance actually works now; 1.3.1 fixed it not showing
Bundled the dynamic libraries locally
Added protection against duplicate launches / instances
Removed useless settings, and download page content can now be collapsed
Added scrollbars and light mode
Added a full launcher startup animation, reducing the white screen on launch
Moved the left sidebar to the top and enlarged the UI; polished the download page and added the Java runtime
Added a large set of settings, organized into Game, Download, Appearance, Advanced, and About
Added automatic Java setup, with a configurable download source (thanks, Tsinghua!)
Improved performance, added a startup animation, and improved log-based troubleshooting
Fixed many download list bugs, such as being unable to cancel and leftovers after cancelling
First stable release
